C1_two_subject.easy: In a 2014 study, psychologist Asifa Majid and linguist Niclas Burenhult asked speakers of Jahai, a hunter-gatherer language of the Malay Peninsula, to name a series of colors and odors, and found that the Jahai named odors as concisely and consistently as colors, typically using abstract smell terms. English speakers, ______ struggled to name the odors, producing lengthy descriptions that usually identified a probable source.
C2_belief_finding.easy: Because few surviving books from before the twelfth century bear the names of women, historians long assumed that medieval Europe’s illuminated manuscripts were produced almost exclusively by monks. ______ in 2019, researchers examining the dental calculus of a woman buried around 1100 at a German women’s monastery discovered particles of lapis lazuli, a costly blue pigment reserved for luxurious manuscripts, and concluded that she had probably painted such texts herself.
C3_limiting_fact.easy: Through the 1930s and early 1940s, Chinese American cinematographer James Wong Howe was among Hollywood’s most sought-after camera artists, prized for his dramatic low-key lighting and pioneering use of deep focus. ______ after being named in testimony as a Communist sympathizer, Howe was gray-listed in the late 1940s and struggled to find studio work until director Samuel Fuller hired him in 1950.
E1_consequence.easy: Until the mid-2000s, Seville, Spain, had virtually no cycling infrastructure, and bicycles accounted for a negligible share of urban trips. Between 2006 and 2010, the city built a continuous 120-kilometer network of cycleways physically segregated from motorized traffic. ______ cycling in Seville increased roughly sixfold, and by 2011 residents were making more than 70,000 bicycle trips on a typical weekday.
E2_motive_action.easy: Observations at the grounding zone of Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier, where the ice detaches from the seafloor and begins to float, are essential for understanding the glacier’s retreat, but the zone lies beneath hundreds of meters of ice that no ship can penetrate. ______ in early 2020, a team including Cornell University scientist Britney Schmidt lowered Icefin, a slender robotic submersible, through a borehole nearly 600 meters deep.
P1_purpose_aptness.easy: The Montessori method, followed at Fuji Kindergarten in Tachikawa, Japan, holds that young children learn best when they are free to move and explore on their own initiative. ______ architect Takaharu Tezuka designed the school’s building, completed in 2007, as a continuous oval ring whose classrooms are separated by movable wooden boxes rather than walls and whose roof deck doubles as a playground and running track.
A1_addition.easy: When Pura Belpré joined the New York Public Library in 1921, becoming its first Puerto Rican librarian, she could find almost no Spanish-language books for children. Assigned to branches in Harlem, Belpré established bilingual story hours, often performing traditional Puerto Rican folktales with puppets. ______ she purchased Spanish-language books for the library’s collections and organized community celebrations of Three Kings Day.
X1_example.easy: A number of contemporary West African artists construct monumental works from discarded consumer goods, transforming the region’s everyday waste into commentary on consumption and scarcity. ______ Ghanaian artist Serge Attukwei Clottey cuts yellow plastic jerrycans, originally imported to hold cooking oil and later used to store water during shortages, into small tiles that he binds with copper wire into enormous tapestries.
S1_spec_restate.easy: Enacted by the US Congress in 1990, the Indian Arts and Crafts Act is a truth-in-advertising law that regulates how art and craft products may be marketed throughout the country. ______ the act prohibits offering, displaying, or selling any such product in a manner that falsely suggests it was made by a member of a federally or state-recognized tribe or by an artisan certified by a tribe.
M1_emphasis.easy: The Epic of Manas, which recounts the exploits of a legendary Kyrgyz hero and his descendants, has been transmitted for centuries by manaschis, specialists who perform it in a melodic chant. Sayakbay Karalaev (1894–1971) was among the most prodigious of these performers. ______ the version transcribed from his recitations between 1936 and 1952 exceeds 500,000 lines, roughly twenty times the combined length of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey.
T1_sequence_time.easy: At the Millennium Seed Bank in West Sussex, England, newly arrived seed collections are first held in a drying room at 15 percent relative humidity for anywhere from two weeks to six months. ______ technicians clean the seeds of debris and X-ray them, discarding any that prove empty or infested. The remaining seeds are dried a second time before being sealed in airtight glass containers and banked in underground vaults at −20°C.
C1_two_subject.medium: In a 2016 study, biologist Jean-Nicolas Audet found that Barbados bullfinches captured in heavily urbanized parts of the island excelled at innovative foraging tasks, such as opening a drawer to obtain food, and also mounted vigorous immune responses. Rural bullfinches, ______ solved such problems less readily and exhibited comparatively weak immunity.
C2_belief_finding.medium: Most animals with a circulatory system rely on a beating heart to propel oxygen-carrying fluid through their tissues. In sea spiders, ______ the heart contracts too feebly to circulate fluid much beyond the center of the body; examining twelve species in 2017, biologist H. Arthur Woods determined that oxygen reaches the animals’ slender legs primarily through peristaltic contractions of gut branches extending into each leg.
E1_consequence.medium: Because red blood cells absorb green light, circulating blood can betray an otherwise translucent frog resting against foliage. In a 2022 study, biologists Carlos Taboada and Jesse Delia found that sleeping glassfrogs withdraw nearly 90 percent of their red blood cells from circulation and sequester them in the liver, whose surface is coated with reflective guanine crystals. ______ the resting frogs become two to three times more transparent.
E2_motive_action.medium: After swollen rivers forced the precautionary evacuation of roughly a quarter of a million people from the eastern Netherlands in 1995, Dutch authorities concluded that continually reinforcing dikes was a losing proposition and that the Rhine and Meuse instead needed space to discharge floodwater safely. ______ the Room for the River program, enacted in 2006, relocated dikes inland, excavated secondary channels, and lowered floodplains at 34 sites.
